content.thinking:
I need to figure out the right symptom framing for the postmortem: the metric tracks the share of purchases categorized confidently, and that share dropped, meaning purchases increasingly got filed without confident categorization. I'm working out how to phrase this as an active, user-facing symptom.

Now I'm building the causal chain: the trigger looks like revision 7c3ca00c deployed to io-shop with the date change from P2, confirmed across replicas, and I need to check whether an earlier deploy (P1) falls inside the metrics window or should be ruled out as a cause.

Series before onset averaged around 89.5% healthy, which fits with P1 having been in place without issue, and the rollback to d268103 restored health and stopped the rule from firing — so P1 is ruled out by the rollback and the alert history, with zero flag changes in that hour confirming no other suspects. That narrows the actual cause to the categoriser.model version bump in the deploy config, which is the only change recorded for that deploy.

Then for why v2 lowered confidence: it likely doesn't lowercase input, so capitalized title words from the shop's categorise function don't match v2's lowercase vocabulary, pushing purchases into an unconfident "General" bucket.

I should also note F1 was run against main rather than 7c3ca00c, and D1's diff only shows the values file changing — meaning categorising.py is identical between that revision and d268103, even though Code-Fix's main isn't literally 7c3ca00c.

The root cause checks out: the shop passes purchase-title words in original case, but model v2 (unlike v1) doesn't lowercase input and its vocabulary was built from lowercased titles, so titles without an all-lowercase match fall through to "General" with low confidence. In plain terms, a configuration change switched the shop to a newer model that likely only recognises lowercase words, while titles were passed unchanged, so many purchases couldn't be confidently categorised.

I note that moving the model back to v2 before a fix runs would likely bring the same drop right back — the repository still points to v2, which explains why. One contributing factor: no test was seen covering v2 on capitalised titles, only on titles already in lowercase.

For this gap, I want to propose an item requiring a categorisation-quality check against new categoriser models before any change to categoriser.model can deploy, rather than leaving that addressed by the merge item whose tests cover a different fault.

CF-2: the model switch hit all replicas simultaneously, with no staged rollout or canary—had a canary existed, the drop would've shown on a fraction first. I'll propose a canary-with-confidence-gate item for model changes.

CF-3: nobody got paged, which is its own finding, but alert routing held fine beforehand and Argus mitigated regardless, so I'm weighing whether this really counts as a contributing factor that would've shortened the incident.

The configuration change not being tied to supporting code (F1, the shop-side prep v2 gap) is root cause territory, not a contributing factor here—skipping it. I'm also noting there's no review gate for model-quality changes, which maps back to CF-1, and drafting an action item for a pre-deploy quality check on categoriser model changes.

I'll add a canary rollout for categoriser.model changes that halts on confident-share drop as a prevent item under CF-2, plus paging on-call for CategorisationConfidenceLow as a detection item. I considered proposing a fix to make the deploy repo say v1 until the real fix lands, but AI-3 already covers that case, so I'll skip it—and since F1's reference commit doesn't match the deployed revision shown in D1, I'm weighing whether to add a verification check for that mismatch, but no item seems needed since Code-Fix already addresses it.

For lessons learned, I'm noting what went well: the Investigator Agent tied the drop to the categoriser's v1-to-v2 move, Argus ruled out flag changes by checking history, Mitigation rolled back and confirmed the service recovered, and Code-Fix proposed draft PR #409. On the went-wrong side, I'm flagging that nobody was paged since no on-call incident was linked to the alert, and that logs weren't read.

For got_lucky, I don't think anything qualifies — requests not failing and rollback being available aren't really luck, so I'll leave that section empty. For assumptions, I'm noting that Code-Fix's read assumes categorising.py at 7c3ca00c matches main, since the diff shows only the values file changed between the two commits, and that what lower confidence meant to users is inferred rather than directly observed, since the record doesn't show the shop UI.

Now I'm drafting step 1, which cites the confidence share dropping well below normal while failure rates stayed flat, and step 2, which cites the deployment revision swapping the categoriser model version in the values file as the only change, with all replicas confirmed on that revision shortly after. I'm also ruling out the prior revision since it was measured healthy before onset and the rollback back to it was later confirmed.

For step 3, I'm noting that model v2 likely couldn't handle capitalized words in purchase titles passed to it as-is, causing confident categorization to fail for many purchases — citing F1 and keeping the phrasing tight rather than fully spelling out the mechanism.

I should avoid writing bare numbers in prose, treating things like PR references as names rather than figures — referring to the draft pull request generically rather than citing its number. For the counterfactual on CF-2, I'm framing that a staged rollout would have exposed the v2 regression on a slice of traffic first, allowing a halt before all purchases were affected.

action_items.item: Add a pre-deploy check that runs any candidate categoriser model on a sample of real purchase titles, kept in their original case, and blocks a change to categoriser.model if the share categorised confidently falls below the current model's.
Roll out changes to categoriser.model in stages, starting with part of the traffic, and halt automatically if the share of purchases categorised confidently falls.
Route CategorisationConfidenceLow on io-shop to the on-call paging rotation so a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Fewer purchases were filed under a category with confidence: the share of purchases categorised confidently fell far below its usual level, and requests failed no more often than usual.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deployment of revision d268103 (P1): the metrics read for the hours before the onset show the service healthy with it in place, and the rollback that put it back in place was confirmed with the alerting rule no longer firing.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider's history showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before the investigation.
A source-code change shipped with the deployment: the diff lists only the production values file, and every other file is as it was at the previous revision.

causal_chain.step: The deployment of revision 7c3ca00c at {P2.1} changed one thing: in deploy/values-production.yaml it moved the categoriser model from v1 to v2 (D1). As of {T10.1}, every replica was running that revision (T10).
Model v2 likely fails to recognise the purchase titles the shop sends it as written, so many purchases came back without a confident category.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A configuration change moved the shop to a newer model for sorting purchases into categories, and that model likely only recognises words written in lower case, while the shop sends it product titles as they are written, so many purchases could not be sorted with confidence.

contributing_factors.factor: No check of categorisation quality on a new model was seen before the model change went out. According to Code-Fix, the existing v2 tests only covered titles whose matching word was already lowercase, so nothing exercised v2 on capitalised titles.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran v2 on real, capitalised purchase titles would have shown the fall in confident categorisation before the change reached production.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The model change reached every replica of io-shop. No staged rollout or canary was seen that would have watched the confident share before the change went everywhere.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout gated on the confident share would have shown the drop on a small part of the traffic and could have stopped the rollout before all purchases were affected.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the deployment's diff and found the move of the categoriser model from v1 to v2.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone else, which kept the investigation on the deployment.
The Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop.
The Mitigation Agent confirmed the rollback once the service was no longer at the incident's level.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request, with a test, for a person to review.

went_wrong: The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it, so no person was called in to the incident.

input.root_cause: According to Code-Fix's reading of the code on main, the shop's categorise function passes purchase-title words to the model in their original case. Model v1 lowercases each word itself, but model v2 does not (lowercases_its_input is False), and v2's vocabulary was built from titles its training pipeline had already lowercased. So under v2, a title with no known all-lowercase word falls through to "General" with confident=False.
input.still_at_risk: Moving the categoriser model back to v2 before a fix runs could bring the same fall in confidently categorised purchases straight back.
input.symptom: Fewer purchases were filed under a confident category
